items.title: Here’s how Google Messages’ in-chat mini games will work
items.summary:
Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Strings of code shed new light on Google’s effort to bring games to the Messages app. 
 You’ll be able to play games, like pool and chess, without leaving the conversation. 
 The feature will support multiplayer gameplay. 
 Notifications will inform users when it’s their turn to play or if they won, lost, or tied. 

Apple often borrows ideas from Android, but the same is true the other way around. For example, Android Authority recently reported that Google has been working on bringing games to the Messages app , similar to the gaming experience in iMessage . At the time, there were no clues on how this feature would work. Now, we can answer some of those questions, thanks to some newly discovered information.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

The new details come from strings of code we spotted while diving into the latest beta (version messages.android_20261113_00_RC00.phone.openbeta_dynamic) of Google Messages. Internally known as “Midnight,” this feature will allow you to play games like pool, chess, checkers, darts, and more. One of the first new strings we came across specifically mentions you’ll be able to play nine classic games without having to leave the conversation.
items.t: Here’s how Google Messages’ in-chat mini games will work

items.title: T-Mobile is reportedly cooking up new prepaid plans, starting at just $20 a month
items.summary:
TL;DR 

T-Mobile is reportedly working on a new line of prepaid plans called T-Select. 
 The plan would have three tiers, at $20, $30, and $40 per month. 
 T-Select is expected to launch in April. 

T-Mobile is reportedly about to add to its prepaid lineup with new plans called T-Select, according to The Mobile Report . The publication’s sources said that there will be three plans for $20, $30, and $40 per month each.

The $20 per month plan would require bringing your own device (BYOD), and includes unlimited talk, text, and data, as well as T-Mobile’s security suite, Scam Shield, and affords access to the T-Mobile Tuesdays perks program. The $30 plan changes that to 10GB of high-speed data, unlimited talk and text, and 5GB of hotspot data. The $40 plan, meanwhile, would have unlimited talk, text, and data (including to Canada and Mexico), as well as 15GB of hotspot data.

items.title: Google Docs solves its Compare tool clutter problem with Word doc support
items.summary:
Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Google has added .docx support to the Compare documents tool. 
 This update allows users to compare .docx files directly in Google Docs without having to convert them first. 
 Support is available for Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal Google accounts. 

Google has started rolling out an update to Calendar that allows you to pick which end of a meeting you want to put your five-minute buffer on. However, that’s not the only Workspace-related update that’s available today. The tech giant is also rolling out a Docs update that makes comparing documents more convenient.

While Google Docs allows you to view and edit Microsoft Office files without converting them first, that wasn’t true if you wanted to use the Compare documents tool. Not only did this force you to convert the file, but it also resulted in you having unnecessary duplicate files in your Google Drive. Those problems are being solved with the rollout of .docx support for the Compare documents tool.
items.t: Google Docs solves its Compare tool clutter problem with Word doc support

items.title: Google expands Gemini’s voice options with 66 new regional accents
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google is rolling out 66 new regional voices to the Gemini app on Android and iOS. 
 The expansion covers seven language variants, including US English, with more than 10 voices available for UK English alone. 
 Your chosen voice applies to both Gemini Live conversations and spoken responses in regular chats. 

When Amazon-owned Ring wanted its video doorbells to feel a little more familiar to customers in Scotland, it launched a nationwide search for someone to record greetings in a Scottish accent. The idea was simple: hearing a familiar voice when you interact with technology can make the experience feel more personal. Google is now bringing that same idea to Gemini , only this time, you’ll be able to hold an entire conversation with an AI that speaks with a local accent.

Google first teased regional voices for Gemini at I/O in May, and the company is now rolling out 66 new voice options to the Gemini app on Android and iOS. These cover seven language variants: US English, UK English, Indian English, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, Indonesian, and Korean.
items.t: Google expands Gemini’s voice options with 66 new regional accents

items.title: Google Maps expands Ask Maps with itineraries, list search, and appointment booking
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google Maps Ask Maps adds itinerary creation, list search, and appointment booking. 
 The update rolls out today, with some features available only in the US. 
 Google is expanding Ask Maps to over 30 countries in Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK. 

Google Maps introduced Ask Maps to help casually answer questions using Gemini, and now it’s getting three new features that help you make an itinerary, search your lists, and schedule appointments. With air travel more unpredictable than ever, it’s likely more people will be hitting the road instead of taking to the skies this holiday season, so these upgrades come at a good time.

Planning an itinerary with Ask Maps can cover an afternoon of hitting stores to finish up all your holiday shopping or a multiday trek across several states. No matter what type of trip you’re setting up, Ask Maps will put numbered pins on the map for each stop along the way. For long excursions, it can create a schedule for each day with recommendations and tips for every stop. After everything is set up, you can share the plans with others, or if you love seeing an itinerary on a page, export it to Google Docs.
items.t: Google Maps expands Ask Maps with itineraries, list search, and appointment booking

items.title: Google Calendar now lets you choose where to put your five-minute meeting break
items.summary:
Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Google Calendar users can now configure the event durations of their Speedy meetings. 
 You can choose between starting five minutes later or ending five minutes earlier. 
 The gradual rollout is starting today for Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal Google accounts. 

It can be hard to find time in your day to relax when you have back-to-back meetings. With Google Calendar’s Speedy meetings feature, however, you can sneak breaks into your busy schedule by shortening the default duration of your event. This feature previously only let you end meetings early, but now you’ll have more choice over where you want to insert your break.

Google is starting to roll out an update for Calendar’s Speedy meetings feature. This update will let the user choose whether new meetings start five minutes later or end five minutes earlier. You’ll also be able to set your default meeting buffer per calendar.
items.t: Google Calendar now lets you choose where to put your five-minute meeting break

items.title: Morphe v2.3.0 update unlocks 1440p and 4K YouTube downloads that even Premium doesn’t offer
items.summary:
Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Morphe v2.3.0 brings native in-app YouTube downloads up to 1440p and 4K (2160p), surpassing official YouTube Premium’s 1080p cap. 
 A new “Show download in video menus” setting adds download options to Premium-restricted videos, while downloads can now resume from their saved position and export directly to your device’s Downloads folder. 
 YouTube Music gains native offline downloads that preserve SponsorBlock skips and more with this Morphe release. 

Morphe , the popular community-driven project based on prior work from ReVanced that lets users customize YouTube and other Android apps, has received a major v2.3.0 update that pushes offline capabilities beyond the 1080p quality official YouTube Premium subscribers get. The headline addition brings native in-app video downloads all the way up to 1440p and 4K (2160p), alongside an option to force these higher resolutions on older or lower-end phones that would normally be restricted.
items.t: Morphe v2.3.0 update unlocks 1440p and 4K YouTube downloads that even Premium doesn’t offer

items.title: One UI 9.5 may let you set a custom greeting for Call Screening
items.summary:
TL;DR 

An early build of One UI 9.5 contains references to an upgraded version of Call Screening that would let users set custom greetings. 
 Call Screening currently lets you change the voice or tweak the speech rate, but doesn’t let you type in a custom greeting. 
 Samsung introduced Call Screening with the Galaxy S26 series earlier this year to answer incoming calls on the user’s behalf. 

Samsung introduced Call Screening with the Galaxy S26 series earlier this year, and One UI 9.5 could make it more customizable. Call Screening can answer incoming calls on your behalf and give you a text transcript of the conversation as it happens. While it lets you change the language, voice, or speech rate, you can’t modify the greeting message that callers hear. Samsung’s next One UI release may change that.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Digging into an early One UI 9.5 build, we have uncovered a handful of strings that reference the ability to modify the opening message incoming callers hear with Call Screening enabled. While we couldn’t surface visuals of this Call Screening upgrade, code strings suggest users can type their own greeting.
items.t: One UI 9.5 may let you set a custom greeting for Call Screening

A new leak claims Samsung could bring variable aperture cameras to the Galaxy S28 Pro and Galaxy S28 Ultra in 2028. 
 The potential comeback follows Apple introducing a variable aperture camera on the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and similar interest from Chinese Android brands. 
 Samsung is expected to skip the hardware on early 2027’s Galaxy S27 series due to added cost and device thickness. 

Samsung last shipped a mechanical variable aperture camera on the Galaxy S10 series in 2019, and rumors of a comeback have circulated since late last year , as Apple’s plans to ship a variable aperture camera on the iPhone became clearer. While earlier evidence suggested Samsung was testing the hardware again , later reports indicated the upcoming Galaxy S27 lineup would skip the upgrade because of added cost and thickness. Now, a new leak points to the Galaxy S28 series as the likely target for the feature’s return.

According to leaker Yogesh Brar on X , variable aperture cameras could make a comeback on the Galaxy S28 Pro and Galaxy S28 Ultra.

The Google Pixel Tag is here and, at least so far, it’s really good. But fresh hardware and some new features can’t fix the core problem. Google’s Find Hub network has been restricted from the very start, and it’s not something Google can easily fix.
